title: Eye-XAI: an explainable artificial intelligence approach for eye disease detection using symptom analysis.
summary: Primary BMC Med Inform Decis Mak Methods/Results use 563 patients referred to ophthalmologists, with disease labels and symptom annotations, and evaluate ML/XAI in train/test and cross-validation. Reported 99.11% accuracy; single Bangladesh cohort and extensive model tuning make this exploratory. The bibliographic records retrieved do not state an author affiliation.
ai_technology: Tree/boosting classifiers and SHAP explain symptom-based predictions across five ophthalmic diagnoses.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: 563 ophthalmologist-diagnosed patients; highest reported classifier accuracy 99.11%, with a clinician reviewing feature explanations.
evidence.unknown: Primary BMC Med Inform Decis Mak Methods/Results use 563 patients referred to ophthalmologists, with disease labels and symptom annotations, and evaluate ML/XAI in train/test and cross-validation. Reported 99.11% accuracy; single Bangladesh cohort and extensive model tuning make this exploratory. Internal splits/cross-validation only and no external validation; modest, imbalanced dataset and extensive tuning mean reported accuracy may be optimistic. Clinician checked SHAP explanations, not independent outcome verification.
evidence.ai_role: Tree/boosting classifiers and SHAP explain symptom-based predictions across five ophthalmic diagnoses.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
